chosen.premise: Touching one of Ninetales' tails can curse you—and your descendants—for 1,000 years.
chosen.hook: Touch one tail, and your family may suffer for a millennium.
chosen.visualIdea: A hand reaches toward a tail as a 1,000-year curse spreads through generations.
chosen.note: A highly specific Ninetales-only threat with strong multi-generation visuals. The Red/LeafGreen entries support the tail curse, while Ultra Sun explicitly adds descendants and 1,000 years.

candidates.premise: Alolan Ninetales keeps the same 1.1-meter height and 19.9-kilogram weight but changes from Fire to Ice/Fairy.
candidates.hook: Same size, same weight—but Ninetales changes its entire type identity.
candidates.visualIdea: A stat card holds height and weight steady while the type icons switch from Fire to Ice and Fairy.
candidates.note: An excellent concrete comparison with exact unchanged measurements and a dramatic Fire-to-Ice/Fairy switch, though regional-form type changes are a somewhat familiar Pokémon format.

candidates.premise: Ninetales' nine tails supposedly hold nine different powers, matching legends of nine beings becoming one.
candidates.hook: Ninetales may be nine supernatural beings fused into one Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Nine glowing tails split into nine silhouettes before merging into Ninetales.
candidates.note: Strongly tied to Ninetales and visually clear, but it combines separate legends rather than establishing one definite rule; the nine tails having unique powers is explicitly framed as a legend.

candidates.premise: Ninetales understands human speech, controls minds with its eyes, and hypnotizes foes with flames.
candidates.hook: Ninetales can understand you—and then hypnotize you.
candidates.visualIdea: Speech bubbles become red eye beams, then flickering flames surround a hypnotized opponent.
candidates.note: The combination of understanding speech, mind control, and flame hypnosis is well supported and cinematic, but it is a bundle of abilities rather than one sharply defined premise.

candidates.premise: Vulpix becomes Ninetales by using a Fire Stone, not by reaching a level.
candidates.hook: Ninetales does not evolve at a level—it evolves with a stone.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Vulpix beside a Fire Stone, then flash-cut to its nine-tailed evolution.
candidates.note: Concrete and well supported, but evolution-item angles work for many Pokémon and are familiar to most fans. The method comes from trusted secondary research rather than a Pokédex entry.

candidates.premise: A long-lived Ninetales' fur is said to shine gold, tying its appearance to its thousand-year lifespan.
candidates.hook: For Ninetales, living longer supposedly makes its fur turn gold.
candidates.visualIdea: Ninetales' coat gradually shifts from ordinary fur into a bright, gleaming gold.
candidates.note: The source says a long-lived Ninetales will have fur that shines like gold, but the premise overstates this as a confirmed gradual color transformation. The visual can imply a process the research does not establish.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the curse premise has the best combination of uniqueness, surprise, specificity, visual potential, and direct Pokédex support.
